History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
45-year-old female housekeeper with 3–4 month history of painful, itchy, cracked palmar skin now severe enough to miss work; clinical impression is occupational contact dermatitis; topical steroid and emollient prescribed with advice to wear gloves and follow-up if no improvement in 10–14 days.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Painful, itchy, cracked skin on palms of both hands.  
• Onset & duration: Began approximately 3–4 months ago after changing housekeeping jobs; progressively worsened.  
• Current severity: “Hurts a lot,” preventing work; has missed last 3 days.  
• Distribution: Primarily palms; generalized mild dryness on legs.  
• Associated features: Intermittent pruritus; occasional bleeding only when scratched.  
• Exacerbating factors: Cleaning chemicals; not wearing protective gloves.  
• Relieving factors/trials: Tried OTC E45 cream and an antihistamine—no benefit.  
• Review of systems:  
  – Constitutional: No fever.  
  – GI: No nausea or vomiting; bowels normal.  
  – GU: No urinary symptoms.  
  – Other systems: No additional complaints reported.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – on metformin; no complications discussed.  
• No known history of eczema, dermatitis, asthma, or bowel disease reported.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• OTC E45 emollient – ineffective.  
• OTC antihistamine – ineffective.

Allergies:
• No known drug or other allergies.

Social History:
• Occupation: Hotel housekeeper; frequent exposure to cleaning products; inconsistent glove use.  
• Smoking: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: “A couple of pints” once per week (minimal).  
• No substance use reported.

Family History:
• Diabetes mellitus in family.  
• No known family history of skin disease, asthma, or bowel disorders.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Skin: No formal exam findings documented (consult conducted remotely).  
• Other systems: Not examined/not documented.

Investigations:
• None obtained at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected contact (irritant) dermatitis of palms  
  – Likely triggered by occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals; risk increased by lack of glove use.  
Plan:  
  • Avoid triggers: Must wear protective gloves at all times when cleaning.  
  • Pharmacologic:  
    – Topical steroid cream (potency and regimen not documented) – prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy.  
    – “Stronger emollients” – apply generously 3–4 times daily for at least 2 weeks.  
  • Education: Importance of adherence to glove use and regular moisturization.  
  • Follow-up: Reassess in 10–14 days; return sooner if symptoms worsen or spread.  
  • Consider alternative treatments or referral to dermatology if no improvement.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Vitals, detailed skin exam, complete medication list with doses, allergy verification beyond “no,” immunization status.  
• No internal transcript conflicts detected.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor pauses but overall intelligible.
